headline: North Korea says it tested an AI-guided torpedo

sources.title: North Korea says it tested new torpedo system with AI capabilities (AP News)
North Korea says tested AI-assisted torpedo system (AFP, via Yahoo News)
North Korea claims to have tested an AI-guided 'super-speed' torpedo (The Independent, via Yahoo News)

chunks.text: On October 17, 2026, North Korea's [[state media]] said the country had tested a new [[torpedo]] that uses artificial intelligence. The Korean Central News Agency said the test took place on October 15. It called the weapon a super-speed, [[precisely guided]] torpedo. AI helps the weapon find its [[target]], according to the report. But the report gave no details to {{back up}} the [[claim]]. North Korea has {{stepped up}} its weapons tests in recent weeks.

verbs.correct: To show that something is true
verbs.wrong: To keep the test results secret
verbs.why: Good reporters back up their stories with photos. Scientists back up their claims with data. North Korea gave no details to back up its claim about the AI torpedo.

verbs.correct: To increase the amount of something
verbs.wrong: To film weapons tests for TV
verbs.why: Cities step up police patrols during big events. A coach steps up practice before the big game. North Korea has stepped up its weapons tests in recent weeks.

chunks.text: State media said the test checked the weapon's engine system, which was developed through more than 180 tests over five years. On October 14, the country {{carried out}} its first underwater missile tests in nearly three years. Experts say leader Kim Jong Un is shifting his [[focus]] to the [[navy]]. North Korea also wants to {{build up}} its supply of weapons that can beat [[missile defenses]] in South Korea and Japan.

verbs.correct: To do something that was planned
verbs.wrong: To announce the results of a test
verbs.why: Nurses carry out many tests every morning. Students carry out a survey about school lunches each year. On October 14, North Korea carried out its first underwater missile tests in nearly three years.
Many young workers build up their savings slowly. A good coach builds up a strong group of young players. North Korea wants to build up its supply of weapons that can beat missile defenses.

chunks.text: [[Outside experts]] are more [[cautious]]. A South Korean professor said the test seemed designed to {{show off}} a weapon that is hard to [[detect]]. He said AI could help a torpedo {{tell real targets apart}} from [[decoys]]. Another expert said the program may need more time. At [[high speeds]], a torpedo is noisy, and other ships can {{pick it up}}. North Korea has also been {{playing down}} South Korea's own fast missile test.

verbs.correct: To show something proudly so others notice
verbs.wrong: To make a weapon cheaper to build
verbs.why: He shows off his new car to all his friends. She shows off her engagement ring at work. A professor said the test seemed designed to show off a weapon that is hard to detect.

verbs.correct: To see the difference between things
verbs.wrong: To give each target a new name
verbs.why: Most people tell the twins apart by their hair. Bank workers tell real money apart from fake money easily. A professor said AI could help a torpedo tell real targets apart from decoys.

verbs.correct: To notice a sound or signal
verbs.wrong: To make a loud warning sound
verbs.why: Radar picks up planes from far away. A good microphone picks up every word. At high speeds, a torpedo is noisy, and other ships can pick it up.

verbs.correct: To make something seem less important
verbs.why: A coach often plays down a loss and praises the players. She plays down her illness so her kids do not worry. North Korea has also been playing down South Korea's own fast missile test.

chunks.text: Some experts believe North Korea is improving its [[guidance]] software. But they doubt that its weapons can choose targets on their own. South Korea's military, which often accuses the North of [[exaggerating]] its weapons, did not comment. Analysts say help from Russia may be {{speeding up}} North Korea's progress. Kim has {{cut off}} all talks and [[cooperation]] with South Korea. [[Nuclear talks]] with the United States {{broke down}} in 2019, and the [[stalemate]] has {{dragged on}} since then.

verbs.wrong: To make something cost more money
verbs.why: A new computer speeds up our work. Good weather speeds up building work. Analysts say help from Russia may be speeding up North Korea's progress.

verbs.correct: To stop all contact with someone
verbs.wrong: To place more guards at a border
verbs.why: After a big fight, some people cut off their old friends. Companies cut off business with suppliers who break the rules. Kim Jong Un has cut off all talks and cooperation with South Korea.

verbs.correct: To fail and come to an end
verbs.wrong: To be signed by both leaders
verbs.why: Many marriages break down because of money problems. Business deals often break down at the last minute. Nuclear talks between North Korea and the United States broke down in 2019.

verbs.wrong: To be kept secret for years
verbs.why: Long meetings often drag on for hours. Some strikes drag on all summer. The stalemate in nuclear talks has dragged on since 2019.

mainIdea.s: North Korea says a new torpedo uses AI to find its targets, but it did not explain how. Outside experts are doubtful and warn that the fast weapon may still be too noisy.
mainIdea.why: State media gave no details to back up the claim. Experts doubt the weapons can choose targets alone, and one says the torpedo is noisy.

mainIdea.s: Experts confirm that North Korea's latest underwater weapon can choose and strike ships by itself. They believe the test puts Pyongyang far ahead of Seoul in the race at sea.
mainIdea.why: Close, but the AI claim comes only from state media. Outside experts doubt that North Korea's weapons can choose targets on their own.

mainIdea.s: South Korea has launched a large submarine that can stay below the surface for weeks. Its navy says the boat will patrol the coast and protect fishing crews during storms.
mainIdea.why: This story is about North Korea's claim that AI guides its new torpedo, and about why outside experts are cautious.

tf.s: North Korea says AI helps its new torpedo find its target.
tf.why: State media made this claim, but it gave no details to back it up.

tf.s: State media gave many details to back up its AI claim.
tf.why: It gave no details to back up the claim, and it did not explain how the AI works.

tf.s: North Korea has stepped up its weapons tests in recent weeks.
tf.why: It also carried out its first underwater missile tests in nearly three years.

tf.s: An expert says the fast torpedo is very quiet under water.
tf.why: He says the program may need more time. At high speeds, a torpedo is noisy, and other ships can pick it up.

tf.s: Kim Jong Un has cut off all talks with South Korea.
tf.why: He has stopped all talks and cooperation with South Korea.

tf.s: North Korea and the United States are holding nuclear talks again.
tf.why: Those talks broke down in 2019, and the stalemate has dragged on since then.

lines.text: Did you see that North Korea says it tested a torpedo guided by AI?
I did. What does the AI actually do?
State media says it helps the torpedo find its target. But they didn't give any details to {{back up}} the claim.
So we just have to [[take their word for it]]?
Pretty much. And South Korea's military says the North often exaggerates.
Right. Still, they've really {{stepped up}} their tests lately. They {{carried out}} underwater missile tests the day before.
Why all the attention on the sea?
Experts say Kim Jong Un is shifting his focus to the navy. One professor thinks they wanted to {{show off}} a weapon that's hard to detect.
Could AI really make it that smart?
He says it might help it {{tell real targets apart}} from decoys.
And what do other experts think?
Another one says it may need more time. A fast torpedo is noisy, and ships can {{pick it up}}.
Could be. And [[to make matters worse]], nuclear talks with the U.S. {{broke down}} in 2019.
And that stalemate has {{dragged on}} ever since.
Kim has also {{cut off}} all talks with South Korea.
That's not good news for anyone hoping for peace.

expressions.def: Used to say you must believe what people tell you without any proof
ex: We can't visit the hotel first, so we have to take their word for it.

expressions.def: Used to say you will believe something only when you see it yourself
ex: He says he cleaned his room, but seeing is believing.

expressions.def: Used to say that someone talks a lot but does not really act
ex: He says he will run a marathon, but he's all talk.
The company promised big changes, but it was all talk.

expressions.def: Used to add one more fact that makes a bad situation worse
ex: The bus was late, and to make matters worse, it started to rain.
I lost my keys. To make matters worse, my phone died.
